To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the quantitative signal obtained from RSI-MR imaging, the cellularity Index, is associated with Gleason grade (a measure of prostate tumor aggressiveness) in prostate cancer at the voxel level within clinically demarcate prostate cancer regions.
RSI-MRI can detect differences in tumor grade at the voxel-level, and that this information could potentially be useful in planning targeted therapies.
RSI-MRI can distinguish between prostate cancer (PCa) and benign tissue and between PCa with low-grade (GG3) and high-grade (GG4+) tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new MRI method for the diagnosis of prostate cancer, which is called restriction spectrum imaging (RSIMRI).
the development of new methods for the detection, diagnosis, and treatment of cancer.
the development and application of novel magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) methods that can be used to improve prostate cancer detection and characterization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
voxel-level RSI-MRI is a valid and reproducible method for assessing tumor cellularity and grade.
the RSI-MR cellularity index is a reliable and reproducible measure of the histopathologic cellularity of prostate cancer, and is associated with GG.
the RSI-MR cellularity index can be used to differentiate between prostate cancer and normal tissue and between low-grade and high-grade tumors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the voxel-level radiologic–pathologic validation of the cellularity index with Gleason grade in prostate cancer is a very important step forward in the field of cancer imaging.

RSI-MRI is able to distinguish between prostate cancers with different GGs at a voxel level, which is important because this information can potentially be used to plan targeted procedures where the most aggressive tumor is targeted.
RSI-MRI is a novel imaging technique that can be used to detect and characterize prostate cancer with a precision that is not currently possible using other MRI techniques.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have demonstrated a correlation at the voxel level between RSI-MRI and Gleason grade, which is the most important prognostic factor in prostate cancer.
the RSI-MR cellularity index can differentiate between prostate cancer and noncancerous prostate tissue.
RSI-MRI is a promising technique for the detection of prostate cancer and for the detection of the more aggressive forms of the disease.
